reason: At the base revision REGEX_FORMAT still matches Y{1,4} while format() only implements YY/YYYY, so 'Y' and 'YYY' fall through to the timezone-offset fallback and return strings like '+0000' instead of the literal 'Y' / '24Y', exactly the bug the PR describes.
After the change REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY, so a lone 'Y' passes through literally and 'YYY' becomes the two-digit year plus a leftover literal 'Y' ('24Y'), matching the expected result.

The base code in #getDecodedParam already decodes params containing '%' via tryDecodeURIComponent, so a %20 path parameter is decoded to a space; the PR is a behavior-preserving refactor of that same check.
The refactored tryDecodeURIComponent performs the identical 'contains %' check before decoding, so percent-encoded route parameters are still decoded to their original characters after the PR.

Before the fix, reschedule writes the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so reading score/at on the held entry reference returns the stale pre-reschedule values, which is precisely what the test checks.
The added @score = at.to_f after the zincrby keeps the in-memory SortedEntry in sync, so the same object reference now reports the newly requested reschedule time immediately.

Parsing 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' with a readable charset parameter is long-standing ContentType behavior; the PR only touches Range header parsing (parseRangesSpecifier), leaving this path unaffected at base.
The Range-header whitespace fix does not touch ContentType parsing, so a charset parameter is still recognized and readable after the PR exactly as before.

The PR only changes error/warning message wording in ComposerRepository download logging and does not touch the archiver; zip creation stores source file modification times, so extracted timestamps should match the originals at base.
Re-archiving behavior is unchanged by the logging-only PR, and zip entries created from the source files carry the files' real modification times rather than a 1980-01-01 default on both extractions.
The CredentialCache prefix-comparison change is unrelated to System.Text.Json; async deserialization of a list with a nullable reference-type property is ordinary supported behavior at this revision.
The PR touches only System.Net credential cache matching, so synchronous and asynchronous JsonSerializer deserialization remain equivalent for a nullable parent property payload.
The cursor FETCH FIRST fix does not touch INET operators or ANY handling, which are long-standing core SQL features, so the <<= ANY containment comparison should parse and return true at base.
The sql_cursor.go change is unrelated to INET operator parsing, so >>= ANY over an INET array should still execute and return true at head without a syntax error.

Before the fix, NO_PROXY='::1' is turned into the wildcard pattern 'all://*:::1', which the URL parsing step cannot interpret and raises an error during client construction, exactly the bug the PR describes.
After the fix, '::1' is recognized as an IPv6 hostname and mapped to 'all://[::1]' with no mount, so client construction succeeds and normal requests still work.

At base, the strict flag-equality check rejects any flag other than IGNORECASE: passing re.DOTALL via flags= or a compiled pattern raises ValueError ('conflicting flags'), so the match call is rejected instead of returning results.

The fix restores support for non-IGNORECASE flags both via flags= and compiled patterns across object, string, and Arrow dtypes, so 'a.c' with DOTALL matches 'a\nc' and not 'ac' in both invocation styles.

This is the celery issue #8890 scenario: freezing a chain with a group in the middle and more tasks after it leaves stale result parents, so the serialized/reconstructed result tree loses child results for the parallel groups at base.
The added prev_task/prev_res bookkeeping keeps result parents correct across mid-chain groups, so serializing and reconstructing the async result preserves all four group child results after the fix.

At base any bare '--' switches the parser into trailing-values mode and is consumed as an escape, so the value_terminator never fires: the first positional keeps capturing '--check' and the second positional stays empty, failing the expected split.

After the fix, when the current positional's value_terminator matches the '--' token, positional parsing handles it, so the first positional stops at value1/value2 and the second collects '--check' without a parse error.

At base the automatic background update calls nvim_set_option_value, and a post-startup (after VimEnter) OSC 11 response triggers OptionSet — the very behavior the PR documents as occurring — along with the ColorScheme reapplication, so both autocommands fire.

After the fix the automatic background update uses ':noautocmd set background=', which deliberately suppresses the OptionSet (and related ColorScheme) events for post-startup OSC 11 responses, so the registered autocommands no longer fire.

Required-field validation flagging an omitted mandatory field as invalid with a 'can't be blank' error is core, long-standing Ecto changeset behavior; the PR only reorders compile-time attribute reads in Ecto.Schema and does not affect runtime validation.
The compile-time derive/Inspect reordering has no effect on changeset casting or validate_required at runtime, so the changeset is still reported invalid with a 'can't be blank' error after the PR.
